message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $423 and own Virginia, Kentucky, and Illinois. I am at INCOME_TAX. Player 1 has a light blue monopoly with hotels on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut. I have no houses or monopolies.

Player 3 holds a dark blue monopoly with Boardwalk and Park Place, plus cash of $566. Player 1 also owns Indiana, blocking my red monopoly. Player 4 has a partial set.

Player 4 is the richest with $701 and two railroads. Unowned properties include Tennessee, B&O Railroad, Marvin Gardens, Pacific, and Short Line. I still have $423 after paying income tax.

Player 1's light blue hotels charge $550 to $600 in rent. Player 3 can build houses on their dark blue properties for about $400 total, raising rent from $35 to $175 on Park Place and $50 to $200 on Boardwalk.

Player 3 can build one house on each dark blue property for $400, leaving $166. Even building costs require placing the same number of houses on every property in the set.

Player 3's dark blue rent is manageable with my cash. I should buy Tennessee if I land on it to block Player 4's orange set. My main goal is acquiring Indiana from Player 1 to complete the red monopoly. They rejected a $250 offer last turn and now have only $165 cash, though their hotels still generate income. Building houses on the red set would cost about $450 per level.

I cannot build houses on the red set yet. Paying $250 for Indiana would leave me with only $173, so I would be more vulnerable rather than safer. I am mapping the board to see where I will land next from Income Tax.

Rolling a 2 from Income Tax lands on Oriental with its hotel for $550. A roll of 4 reaches Vermont with its hotel for $550. A roll of 5 reaches Connecticut with its hotel for $600. The probability of hitting any light blue hotel next turn is roughly 8/36.

Mortgaging all three properties would raise $310, enough to cover a hotel hit. I should not mortgage preemptively. I will stay liquid and avoid trading now.

Mortgaging all four properties would raise $420, so the maximum I can pay for Indiana and still survive a $600 hotel hit is $243. Player 1 rejected a $250 offer last turn, so trading for Indiana is impossible without going broke. I cannot trade for Tennessee because it is unowned. Trading with Player 3 would be risky since they hold a dark blue monopoly.

I cannot complete a pink monopoly with Player 3 or Player 4. Player 3 spent $450 and will build dark blue houses, so I should not help them. Player 4 needs Tennessee to finish an orange set, which I should block. I am now looking for a trade that would hurt Player 1 or Player 3 instead.

I will end the turn. I cannot trade for a pink monopoly without St. Charles, and Player 1 only has two reds. I am staying liquid to survive hotel hits and buy Tennessee.

Player 1's single green property generates only $12 in rent, so they pose little threat. Player 3 will build houses on their dark blue set next turn. I rejected offering Virginia to Player 1 because it would lose my pink block. Player 3 has no incentive to stop building.

I will end the turn. I am weighing a public message to Player 3 warning them that one house on the dark blues is all their cash buys, or staying silent.
